observations_from_original_source: sqlite3_initialize runs before acquiring the static PRNG mutex; its nonzero result returns without resetting or generating bytes.
N<=0 or NULL destination changes only s[0] to0 while holding the mutex; cached output, n and other state words remain unchanged.
Initialization calls sqlite3_vfs_find before writing the four constants. OS entropy writes44 bytes to s[4..14]; then s[15]=s[12], s[12]=0 and n=0.
Each new ChaCha20 block uses a wrapping preincrement of s[12]. Short reads copy out[n-N..n), whereas exhausting a cached remainder copies out[0..n).
PRNG save/restore copies the entire state object; selected x86_64 layout is132 bytes including three zero-initialized padding bytes.

The Unix VFS entropy implementation uses zero-fill, actual PID, robust_open /dev/urandom, READ retry only on EINTR, robust_close, and a time/PID fallback. It is not equivalent to blindly substituting getrandom.
unixGetTempname has separate temp-directory, mutex, formatting, collision count and access semantics. This author does not claim that separate owner exists.
